newsitem.title: USA: Capital equipment makers boosted by Deere comments.
newsitem.headline: Capital equipment makers boosted by Deere comments.

text.p: Deere & Co's outlook for strong agricultural and construction markets for the next several months was lifting the entire construction and farming equipment sector Tuesday.
"The broad-based nature of their optimism was somewhat of an upside suprise for people," Lisa Shalett, analyst at Sanford C. Bernstein, said.
Deere said it expected the remainder of fiscal 1997, ending in October, would benefit from a growing global economy, healthy agriculture markets and high levels of farmer confidence.

"Industrial retail demand for construction equipment is strong and is expected to remain at similar levels throughout 1997 as favorable economic growth, rising incomes and low inflation rates continue to result in good housing demand," Moline, Illinois-based Deere chief executive officer Hans Becherer said in a news release.
Those factors not only helped boost Deere to a new 52-week high Tuesday, but were also helping lift Caterpillar Inc, Case Corp and AGCO Corp, analysts said.

"Clearly the company that would benefit most directly from the trends that Deere noted is Case," said J. Blair Brumley, analyst with Dain Bosworth Inc. Racine, Wisconsin-based Case operates in similar construction and farming equipment markets as Deere, he noted.

Deere reported earnings Tuesday for the second quarter of $1.25 a share, up from $1.04 a year ago and exceeding the First Call consensus estimate of $1.15 a share. Total equipment net sales were $3.1 billion for the quarter, which ended April 30, compared to $2.7 billion a year ago.
"The influences that are driving those revenue performances at Deere should be readily applicable for Case as well," Brumley said.
Case shares were up 1-3/4 at 57-1/2 Tuesday. Deere set a new 52-week high of 52 and was up 2-1/8 at 51-1/8 in afternoon trading.
Caterpillar, the Peoria-based capital equipment maker, also reached a fresh 52-week high, up 1-1/4 to 97-1/2.
And Duluth, Georgia-based AGCO Corp, an agricultural equipment maker, was near its 52-week high, up 1-5/8 to 31-1/4.

Roger Sit, analyst at Goldman Sachs, said many of the capital equipment makers are trading at a discount to the market, due to market assumptions that the current U.S. economic cycle is nearing its end.
Using an analogy of a baseball game, Sit said Deere's comments might help convince the market the economic cycle that has helped boost these companies is not about to end.
"I'm in no way advocating that we're in the first inning in the ballgame, but we're not in the ninth inning," Sit said.
